overall_reason: Textbook default SaaS page: sparkle pill, indigo-to-fuchsia gradient headline, a drawn browser window with a fake bar chart, a greyed logo strip of invented brands, three emoji feature cards under "Everything you need to grow", a five-star quote from "Sarah Chen", three pricing tiers with "Most popular", and a gradient CTA band; one witty line in the sub-head does not change the skeleton.

findings.evidence: Failed T-STOCK-ORDER with 7 stock sections in stock order: hero with product mock -> logo strip ("Trusted by 4,000+ indie teams") -> three equal feature cards -> testimonial -> three pricing tiers -> closing CTA band ("Stop guessing. Start knowing.") -> footer.
findings.before: hero mock, logos, 3 features, quote, 3 tiers, CTA band, footer
findings.after: Lead with one real funnel from a real product, annotated (where users dropped, what the replay showed); fold features into that walkthrough; keep pricing; cut the logo strip and CTA band
findings.why: Seven stock sections in stock order is a generated page however good any one line is.

findings.evidence: Logo strip is styled text of invented or placeholder brands: "ACME ▸ FATHOM ▸ BASELINE ▸ RADAR ▸ PROMPTLY" (Acme is the canonical placeholder company; Fathom is a real analytics competitor). Testimonial: "— Sarah Chen, founder of Stitchboard" with ★★★★★, a default-cast name with no photo, link or date. The sweep's default_names detector did not fire.
findings.before: ACME / FATHOM / ... ; "Sarah Chen, founder of Stitchboard" ★★★★★
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: real customer names with permission and a real quote], or remove both blocks
findings.why: Invented customers and a default-cast reviewer are fabricated proof; naming a real competitor as a customer is worse.

findings.evidence: A div browser window with red/yellow/green traffic-light dots containing eight gradient bars with no axis, labels, values or title. T-DELETION: removing it loses no fact; it shows nothing about funnels, cohorts or replay.
findings.before: fake browser chrome + unlabeled bar chart
findings.after: A real screenshot of a funnel view, or [DATA NEEDED: product screenshot]; drop the window dots (SLP-168)
findings.why: Imitation product UI with no data is decoration posing as the product.

findings.where: h1, section h2s and CTA band
findings.evidence: Failed T-RIVAL-NAME: "Know exactly what your users do.", "Everything you need to grow", "Simple pricing", "Stop guessing. Start knowing." all stay true under PostHog, Mixpanel or Amplitude. T-FRESH-READER generic lines: these four plus "Join 4,000+ founders who understand their product."
findings.after: Build the head from the one specific idea already on the page: analytics for indie founders without a data team or "a second mortgage", e.g. a head that states the price-and-setup difference
findings.why: The hero and every section head are category boilerplate.

findings.evidence: Pill above the headline "New · AI Insights ✨" (sparkle emoji, an unrelated AI feature announcement on an analytics page), a two-tone indigo-violet-fuchsia gradient h1, a lavender radial wash behind it, all centred (SLP-150).
findings.before: sparkle pill + gradient-text h1 + radial wash
findings.after: Drop the pill and the wash; set the h1 in solid ink; left-align the hero with the product view beside it
findings.why: Pill, gradient headline and glow are the three hero tells that together say 'generated'.

findings.evidence: Invented-precision proof beyond the sweep's "Trusted by 4,000+" hit: "We found the exact step where users churned in a 15-minute session. Skittie paid for itself in one afternoon." and "Join 4,000+ founders" in the CTA band, plus "Most popular" on Pro with no basis.
findings.before: "Skittie paid for itself in one afternoon." / "Most popular"
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: sourced customer count and a real quote]; show "Most popular" only if true (INT-186)
findings.why: Unsupported proof claims are integrity failures, not style.

strengths: The sub-head has one real voice line worth keeping: "Funnels, cohorts and session replay that don't require a data team — or a second mortgage."
Pricing tiers state concrete limits (10k / 500k / 5M events per month, 7-day vs unlimited retention).
not_investigated: Inter was shimmed in capture; render assumed close to intended.
